plan: This auction functions like a second-price auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid (the clock stops when the second-highest bidder exits at their sealed bid). With independent private values and no information about others' bids, the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. This ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' values, paying only the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit without risk of overpaying.

This auction structure (sealed bid as exit price in ascending clock) is equivalent to a second-price auction. In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' behavior - it maximizes expected profit. Bidding higher risks winning and losing money if I overpay relative to my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $34, I should bid exactly $34 to ensure I only win when profitable and pay the efficient second-highest price.

Since this is effectively a second-price auction (the sealed bid acts as an exit price in an ascending clock, meaning the winner pays the second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. There's no benefit to bidding above or below my true valuation of $45.
